newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Catholic is British preacher of the year.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Catholic is British preacher of the year.

text.p: A 65-year-old Roman Catholic priest from Scotland became Britain's Preacher of the Year on Wednesday, seeing off four rivals in front of a packed house at Southwark Cathedral in central London.

With the reclining bronze figure of one-time parishioner William Shakespeare looking on, Father Bill Anderson, canon of St Mary's Cathedral, Aberdeen, took the award with a sermon about the battle between pride and humility in the believer.

"The true martyr is he who has become the instrument of God, who has lost his will in the will of God, and who no longer desires anything for himself, not even the glory of being a martyr," he said, quoting T.S. Eliot on Saint Thomas a Becket.
The competition, held for the first time last year, was organised by the College of Preachers which provides courses for people from all the mainstream Christian churches.
It was sponsored by The Times newspaper, nicknamed "The Thunderer" for its fire and brimstone editorials of old.

Last year there was a cash prize. But, according to one of the organisers, the Methodists felt it was wrong to offer a monetary incentive for preaching God's word, so this year the winner got a sculpture of a dove representing the Holy Spirit. One Methodist was in contention this time, 70-year-old Arnold Kellett, plus Anne Peat, 48, the sole woman, described as an Anglican/Methodist.
Peat called for Christians to evangelise amongst the young using the music of youth, and -- "Dare I say it in present company?" -- amongst women using "inclusive language".
That seemed to be a jibe at one of the judges, environment minister John Gummer, who quit the Church of England over his opposition to women priests and converted to Catholicism.
An Anglican and a minister from the Church in Wales equally adept at preaching in English and Welsh made up the five.
